question: Which year is considered the approximate composition period of the Natya Shastra, the earliest known treatise on Indian music and dance?
solution:
The correct answer is __**200 BCE**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The **Natya Shastra** is the most ancient and comprehensive treatise on the performing arts, including **dance**, **music**, and **drama**. It is traditionally attributed to the legendary sage **Bharata Muni**.

• The approximate period of its composition is widely accepted by historians and scholars to be between **200 BCE and 200 CE**. The year **200 BCE** represents the beginning of this classical period of compilation. ***Hence, the correct answer is 200 BCE.***

• The text is written in **Sanskrit** and is composed of approximately **6000 poetic verses** (shlokas) spread across **36 chapters**. It provides a detailed framework for everything from stage design to the emotional states of actors.

• It is often referred to as the **Pancham Veda** or the **Fifth Veda**. This designation signifies its importance as a sacred text that was intended to be accessible to all sections of society, unlike the four primary Vedas.

• The other options, such as **1000 BCE**, **500 CE**, and **1500 CE**, are historically inaccurate. **1000 BCE** corresponds to the early **Vedic period**, while **500 CE** and **1500 CE** belong to the **Gupta** and **Medieval** periods respectively, which are much later than the linguistic and cultural context of the **Natya Shastra**.

**Additional Information__**

__

• **Rasa Theory**: The **Natya Shastra** is famous for introducing the concept of **Rasa** (aesthetic essence or sentiment). It lists **eight primary Rasas**: **Shringara** (Love), **Hasya** (Mirth), **Karuna** (Compassion), **Raudra** (Anger), **Veera** (Heroism), **Bhayanaka** (Fear), **Bibhatsa** (Disgust), and **Adbhuta** (Wonder).

• **Classification of Music**: The treatise classifies musical instruments into four distinct categories: **Tata Vadya** (stringed instruments), **Avanaddha Vadya** (percussion instruments like **drums**), **Ghana Vadya** (solid instruments like **cymbals**), and **Sushira Vadya** (wind instruments like **flutes**).

• **Dance Elements**: It describes **108 Karanas** (basic dance movements) and various **Mudras** (hand gestures). These elements form the technical foundation for all **Indian Classical Dance** forms such as **Bharatanatyam**, **Odissi**, and **Kathakali**.

• **Theatrical Architecture**: The text provides specific guidelines for the construction of playhouses (**Natyamandapa**), describing three shapes: **Vikrishta** (rectangular), **Chaturasra** (square), and **Tryasra** (triangular).

**Important Points__**

• **Abhinavagupta**: The most influential commentary on the **Natya Shastra** is the **Abhinavabharati**, written by the **Kashmiri** philosopher **Abhinavagupta** in the **10th-11th century CE**. This commentary is essential for modern interpretations of the text.

• **Gandharva Veda**: The musical science described in the **Natya Shastra** is known as **Gandharva**, which is considered an **Upaveda** of the **Sama Veda**. It focuses on the ritualistic and spiritual power of sound.

• **Shrutis and Swaras**: The text establishes the system of **22 Shrutis** (microtones) and the **seven Swaras** (notes: **Sa, Re, Ga, Ma, Pa, Dha, Ni**), which remain the bedrock of **Hindustani** and **Carnatic** classical music.

• **Tandava and Lasya**: It distinguishes between **Tandava** (the vigorous, masculine dance attributed to **Lord Shiva**) and **Lasya** (the graceful, feminine dance attributed to **Goddess Parvati**).
